article_title: The Decline of the Luxury Clothing Industry
news_headline: Apple Unveils First Foldable iPhone Duo, Starting at $1,999
post_text:
On September 9, Apple's new CEO John Ternus unveiled the iPhone Duo, the company's first foldable smartphone, starting at $1,999 and topping out near $3,000. Bloomberg reported that Apple is positioning the device explicitly as a status symbol, a way to signal premium positioning and revive the company's innovator image after years of incremental upgrades.

The pricing move is striking not because a $2,000 iPhone is unthinkable, but because Apple is leaning on price itself as the message. Samsung already sells a flagship fold at roughly the same figure. Matching a competitor on cost while betting that the Apple logo carries a luxury premium is a gamble, and it's a familiar one.

WBR's piece on the decline of the luxury clothing industry makes the case that aggressive price hikes, used to manufacture exclusivity rather than earn it, eventually hollow out a brand. Apple isn't a fashion house, but the logic applies: when the price tag does the work that the product used to do, that's worth watching closely. Read the full WBR analysis to see how that pattern plays out.

#Apple #BusinessStrategy
